result.rationale: The diff replaces the old members action, which defaulted to 200 and only applied limit/offset to automatic groups, with `limit = (params[:limit] || 50).to_i` applied to all groups with no upper clamp. The mechanism is verifiable in the diff: an unauthenticated-authenticated client of /groups/:name/members can pass any limit and force serialization of the entire user table (e.g. trust_level_0), a resource-exhaustion vector introduced by this change.

adjudication.rationale: In `GroupsController#members`, the diff changes pagination to `limit = (params[:limit] || 50).to_i` and applies it unconditionally, with no upper bound, then does `group.users.order(:username_lower).limit(limit).offset(offset)` and serializes the result. This allows a request like `?limit=1000000` to fetch and serialize an extremely large number of users (especially for large/automatic groups like `trust_level_0`). The previous implementation effectively capped automatic-group pagination at 200 via `(params[:limit] || 200).to_i` and did not remove that cap; this change removes any such cap/regression in resource usage control.
